hypothesis: Under DTI with alpha=0.2, beta=0.8 and a 300 m triangular kernel, adding one dot moves the denominator by exactly alpha, so it raises the score exactly when its kernel weight k exceeds alpha*DTI (0.056 at DTI 0.28), i.e. when it lands within ~2.8 px of an unseen fault. Marginal value is therefore a chance-of-nearby-truth test, not a surface-ranking test: a spacing-constrained coverage order should beat top-k ranking at equal budget, and a physics-only model should beat a catalogue-copying model once the organizers' masking of mapped faults is taken into account.
mechanism: 33 catalogue-blind channels from hash-pinned USGS GeoDAWN radiometric/magnetic grids and 3DEP 1 m LiDAR terrain descriptors; HistGradientBoosting trained on visible mapped faults only in each holdout fold; greedy score-ordered coverage order with a 2 px suppression radius, a 300 m exclusion ring around the catalogue and a 55,000-dot budget.
non_fault_mimic: Roads, channels, terrace risers, paleo-shorelines, landslide toes and mine benches all create LiDAR steps; basin-fill and lithologic contacts create magnetic/radiometric lineaments. The LiDAR product's own metadata names the same mimics. No negative-control raster was available with a verifiable hash, so mimic suppression is unverified.

holdout.protocol: SegmentHoldout(buffer 15 px): whole 8-connected catalogue components touching a quadrant collar hidden everywhere; catalogue features rebuilt from visible faults only; visible faults masked pixel-exactly; pooled TP/FP/FN; alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m kernel.

hypotheses.name: SATCOV-MORPH-1 — saturating coverage of a physics-only likelihood surface
hypotheses.layers: 11 LiDAR scarp channels (slope excess, crest/base curvature, up/down-facing step, cross-slope gradient, relief, coherence, strike) + 4 radiometric (K, Th, U, TC) + 4 magnetic (ThK, UK, UTh, TMI up-150 m) + 8 structure-tensor/gradient channels + 6 terrain aggregates = 33 catalogue-blind channels
hypotheses.signature: scarp morphology at 2 m aggregated to 100 m, plus cross-cutting lineaments in magnetics and radiometrics; placed by a spacing-constrained coverage order
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: No catalogue-distance input and no catalogue pixel is emitted, so the model cannot earn credit by reproducing mapped faults — which the organizers mask out of scoring anyway. It has to re-find the physical signature.
hypotheses.status: IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED in this file (HOLDOUT-DTI 0.171866)
hypotheses.cost: one model, ~10 min on 2 CPU cores

hypotheses.name: Mask-aware catalogue proximity (hybrid)
hypotheses.layers: physics surface x (1 + w*exp(-d_catalogue/600 m)) with a 300 m exclusion ring
hypotheses.signature: same physics, re-ordered toward the ~1 km halo where new strands of mapped systems are found
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: It uses proximity only outside the ring, and the ring is exactly where the mapped fault itself sits. Inside the ring a dot is unmasked and charged full price.

hypotheses.name: Thermal corroboration gate
hypotheses.layers: fault-likelihood ridges intersected with the GDR geothermal well/spring inventory, plus volcanic vents
hypotheses.signature: a fault that also hosts a spring, well or young vent
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: A mapped fault already carries its own evidence; the interesting candidates are unmapped traces that nevertheless discharge. This is the sponsor's actual target.
hypotheses.status: NOT VALIDATED. The free official inventory is already fetched (gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv, 2.1 MB) so this is viable without new external data.
hypotheses.cost: low — a spatial join and a second gate

hypotheses.name: Kinematic non-coaxiality between scarp asymmetry and strain-rate dilatation
hypotheses.layers: LiDAR up-facing/down-facing step channels vs the organizer's dilatation- and shear-strain-rate bands
hypotheses.signature: a scarp that faces the wrong way relative to the dilatation gradient is not a fault scarp
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: It is a physical consistency test, so it can reject false scarps anywhere, including far from any mapped fault.
hypotheses.status: BLOCKED ON DATA: the strain-rate bands exist only inside the login-gated training_features.tif, which is not in this checkout. Free official source: https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/data/ (account required).
hypotheses.cost: medium once the file is available

hypotheses.name: Magnetic-source-depth step across basin margins
hypotheses.layers: top-of-crustal magnetic source depth (or an inversion from the available TMI up-150 m grid)
hypotheses.signature: an abrupt depth step across a basin margin marks a buried fault with no surface scarp
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: Buried faults are systematically under-mapped in a surface-fault database, so this is where new labels are most likely to be found.
hypotheses.status: PARTIALLY BLOCKED: the organizer's depth band is login-gated. A free substitute exists (invert the mirrored TMI up-150 m grid) but is unvalidated and was not used here.

limitations: No organizer receipt binds any owner-reported score to bytes.
The shared 19-band organizer feature cache is absent from this checkout; this lane uses hash-verified peer-mirrored GeoDAWN/3DEP products, so provenance is OWNER-MIRROR, not organizer-authenticated.
The holdout truth is the mapped catalogue, not the experts' new-fault labels, and mapped faults are masked at scoring - the holdout measures a related but different quantity.
No negative-control raster (TIGER roads, BLM claims) was hash-pinned, so road/bench suppression is unverified.
One 100 m fault trace is not a geothermal vent.
